content: We performed several text pre-processing steps. First, we tokenized the text using the Farasa Arabic NLP toolkit BIBREF20. Second, we removed URLs, numbers, and all tweet specific tokens, namely mentions, retweets, and hashtags as they are not part of the language semantic structure, and therefore, not usable in pre-trained embeddings. Third, we performed basic Arabic letter normalization, namely variants of the letter alef to bare alef, ta marbouta to ha, and alef maqsoura to ya. We also separated words that are commonly incorrectly attached such as ياكلب> (“yAklb” – “O dog”), is split to يا كلب> (“yA klb”). Lastly, we normalized letter repetitions to allow for a maximum of 2 repeated letters. For example, the token ههههه> (“hhhhh” – “ha ha ha ..”) is normalized to هه> (“hh”). We also removed the Arabic short-diacritics (tashkeel) and word elongation (kashida).
